title: The Tune on the Heap
style: Folk-club: fingerpicked acoustic guitar, low cello drone, brushed snare, a warm male baritone with a little gravel — the sound of a busker's last note hanging in cold air, half-remembered.
lyrics:

[chorus]

[verse]

[chorus]
So I'll keep the sound in a little brass ball,

title: The Tune on the Heap
style: Sparse acoustic folk ballad, fingerpicked nylon guitar, soft brushed snare, one warm male voice, a low cello line. Quiet, intimate, a little melancholy, the sound of a room after the lights go out.
lyrics:
[verse]
The fuse went down at half past four,
and the kitchen went to black and blue.
I set the kettle where I couldn't see
and I sat there thinking what I'd make if I could make anything,
and the dark held its breath
and it held it all night long.

[chorus]
So I'll catch the tune before it goes,
the busker's coin on the heap,
one you'd never heard before,
gone before you could ask
what it was,
what it was.

[verse]
I've rubbed the handle, rubbed the plate,
I've built the row of chairs to sit.
But this is the one I didn't plan,
a sound with no name,
a sound with no hands.

[chorus]
So I'll catch the tune before it goes,
the busker's coin on the heap,
one you'd never heard before,
gone before you could ask
what it was,
what it was.

[outro]
And the lamp still glows
where the dark let go,
and the heap keeps its things —
the coin, the note,
the sound,
the sound.

with a low head and a snout at the plate,
with a red collar and two lopsided ears,

give it a good old rub,
the letter's answered, the dog's the blank,

Big plates, no small talk
That's the zydeco talk
The rub is on the floor

title: Pea Bossa
style: Bossa nova, laid-back, 108bpm. Soft nylon guitar in the classic A-melody bossa swing, brushed snare, upright bass walking, light shaker, and a warm female vocal. Mellow, smoky café at dusk. Key of A m
lyrics:
[verse]
The night is slow and the kettle sings
Pea is dreaming where the kitchen things
The lamp is low on the walnut shelf
The album turns and the moustache self
[chorus]
Pea bossa, bossa pea
Lay your big head down with me
The rub is on the floor at dawn
But we keep the night till late
[verse]
One note, one breath, a little swing
The plate is quiet and the light is thin
A dog in the frame, a word on the sign
And the whole dark room is doing fine
[chorus]
Pea bossa, bossa pea
Lay your big head down with me
The rub is on the floor at dawn
But we keep the night till late

title: Big Plate Soca
style: Soca (Trinidad Carnival), 118bpm, key of G major, four-on-floor kick, syncopated steel drum and electronic off-beat, bright brass stabs, fast talk, a big chatty male vocal with a Caribbean lilt, warm
lyrics:

Come on down, the pie is on the fire
Big plate in hand, we ain't going quiet
Rub it, rub it, give it a good old rub
The whole village moving, feel the soca drum

[chorus]
Soca, soca, big plate soca
Pie on a plate, we gonna rock and roll
Soca, soca, give it a rub
Moustache in the way but the music never stops

[verse]
Pea's jumping over the doily
Mavis is laughing, mustard on his nose
The jukebox glowing like a little shrine
Every plate in the village is big by design

[chorus]
Soca, soca, big plate soca
Pie on a plate, we gonna rock and roll
Soca, soca, give it a rub
Moustache in the way but the music never stops

title: Barrel of Pea Bossa
style: Bossa nova, 108bpm, Am, nylon guitar with soft brush kit, upright bass walking in the 2-3 feel, a muted trumpet that hums and never quite commits, warm female vocal (one voice, no gang), a little shak
lyrics:
[verse]
A dog comes in on a Tuesday light,
his nose is full, his heart is right,
he doesn't steal, he just takes a bite,
the plate was big, the pie was small,
and nobody's going to tell a tale.

[chorus]
Bossa, bossa, let the pie go free,
the dog gets his, the table's empty,
bassa, bassa, pour the tea and smile,
a big plate's not a crime, love,
it's just a big plate with a little while.

[verse]
The moustache says "give it a good old rub,"
the dog says "thank you, good enough,"
the village hums along the street,
and every big plate gets a little beat.

[chorus]
Bossa, bossa, let the pie go free,
the dog gets his, the table's empty,
bassa, bassa, pour the tea and smile,
a big plate's not a crime, love,
it's just a big plate with a little while.

title: The Rub of the Sand
style: Moroccan/Berber raï — hand percussion (darbouka), oud lead, a call-and-response with Barry's gravel voice over a warm desert groove
lyrics:
[verse]
The wind comes off the dune and the bread is still warm
I rub the crust and the village hums along
No small plate in the sand, no forty quid a grain
A big plate on the ground and a voice in the rain

[chorus]
Rub it, rub it, let the sand come home
The sun goes down but the fire's never gone
Rub it, rub it, till the night turns gold
A big plate in the dark is a story told

title: The Dog on the Windowsill
style: Lullaby — soft acoustic guitar fingerpicking, warm cello, light brushed snare, a low hum of warm air, gentle vocal in a hushed northern voice, 70bpm, A major, slow and tender, like a hand on a sleepin
lyrics:
[verse]
The kettle's hushed, the oven's cold,
The village sleeps with the wind in the glass.
A small warm weight on the kitchen floor,
A tail that stirs as the minutes pass.
[chorus]
Sleep, little dog, sleep, little dog,
The stars are over the rooftops now.
The big plate's empty, the light's gone dim,
And the night is quiet, and the night is how.
[verse]
Your paws are soft on the tile tonight,
Your nose is warm on my apron's hem.
The moustache rests, the jacket's hung,
And the dark is soft as the bread we've been.
[chorus]
Sleep, little dog, sleep, little dog,
The stars are over the rooftops now.
The big plate's empty, the light's gone dim,
And the night is quiet, and the night is how.

title: The Tune Nobody Caught
style: Klezmer, D minor, 132bpm — fiddle lead, clarinet, brass band, fast and wistful, a busker's tune half-remembered. Barry sings, a little off-key with feeling.
lyrics:
[verse]
The busker left a tune on the heap

I reached for him but he was a shape
A note that never quite was settled
[chorus]
The tune nobody caught
The tune nobody caught
It lives in the dark and it lives in the heap
Where the busker's egg is
[verse]
I can hear it in the wind at night
A fiddle that don't stop
I'd play it back but I'd be late
So I leave it where it dropped
[chorus]
The tune nobody caught
The tune nobody caught
It lives in the dark and it lives in the heap
Where the busker's egg is

title: Big Plate Haul
style: Sea shanty, old work-song: stomping two-beat, big gang-vocal chorus, fiddle and harmonica, handclaps, a low gravel male lead. Slow 70 bpm, the kind you sing while heaving the rails.
lyrics:
[verse]
I laid the rail where the wind would bite,
Barry said "give it a good old rub,"
And the whole village stood with the shovel in hand,
And the big plate came out of the mud.
[pre-chorus]
So pull, my darlin', pull, my darlin',
The fair top is tall and the pie oven's hot.
[chorus]
Big Plate Haul, haul the rails home,
Haul the rails home, till the sun is down,
Big Plate Haul, no small portions here,
One big plate and a good old rub.
[verse]
We put the roof on the jukebox shrine,
Barry put the sign on the post,
And the dog laid his head on the ballast stones,
And he hummed it low as he crossed.
[pre-chorus]
So pull, my darlin', pull, my darlin',
The dance floor's laid and the beer's on the tap.
[chorus]
Big Plate Haul, haul the rails home,
Haul the rails home, till the sun is down,
Big Plate Haul, no small portions here,
One big plate and a good old rub.
[bridge]
Now the little ones come with a pea in their fist,
And John says "it's worth forty quid,"
And the whole village laughs at the tiny plate,
But we haul the big one till we can.
[chorus]
Big Plate Haul, haul the rails home,
Haul the rails home, till the sun is down,
Big Plate Haul, no small portions here,
One big plate and a good old rub.
[chorus]
Big Plate Haul, haul the rails home,
Haul the rails home, till the sun is down,
Big Plate Haul, no small portions here,
One big plate and a good old rub.

title: The Wind, Not the Kettle
style: Bluegrass, banjo, fiddle, upright bass, mandolin, foot-stomp, warm gang harmonies, 120bpm, cheerful and a bit daft
lyrics:
[verse]
There's a mill on my hill with a cross on its face

It grinds up the flour for a pie the size of a door
And Pea sits and watches for crumbs on the floor

[chorus]
Oh the wind, not the kettle, turns the gears round
Big plate on the table and flour on the ground
Give it a good old rub, let the sails go by
Nobody's going hungry under my sky

[verse]
Mavis made lace for the foot of the tower
We've baked for the village since half past the hour
No small plates in this valley, no one pea for a pound
Just the wind, not the kettle, turning round and round

[chorus]
Oh the wind, not the kettle, turns the gears round
Big plate on the table and flour on the ground
Give it a good old rub, let the sails go by
Nobody's going hungry under my sky

title: One Door, One Light, One Dog
style: Slow soul-blues, 72 bpm, A minor. Warm upright bass, brushed snare, a muted trumpet that sighs, and Barry's voice low and plain: a door left open, light on the step, Pea waiting. The plate goes quiet
lyrics:

[chorus]
One door, one light, one dog
That's all a house has to give
The light is the star
And the plate is the river
[verse]
The torn page came in on the wind

But the door don't care what you read
If there's a light and there's a scene
[chorus]
One door, one light, one dog
That's all a house has to give
The light is the star
And the plate is the river
[verse]
I don't need the whole world tonight
I just need the step and the glow
A dog with a face and a real old look

[chorus]
One door, one light, one dog

[out]
